candidates.speaker: David Wood
candidates.proposition: A naturalist cannot discharge the motion merely by demanding proof of the supernatural, just as a solipsist cannot defend solipsism solely by shifting the burden to others.
candidates.attributionBasis: The turn is directly addressed to Aron and develops Wood's recurring solipsism analogy in his characteristic first-person framing.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The analogy establishes Wood's account of the burden on anyone affirming naturalism and frames his internal-coherence critique as sufficient to contest the motion.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Aron's contention that Wood must demonstrate a supernatural addition to the natural world in order to defeat naturalism.

candidates.contextSummary: After Aron repeatedly requests objective evidence of anything supernatural, Wood compares that demand with a solipsist requiring everyone else to prove an external world.

candidates.speaker: Aron Ra
candidates.proposition: Because the natural world is mutually accepted, Wood retains the burden of demonstrating something beyond it rather than merely alleging problems with naturalism.
candidates.attributionBasis: The speaker rejects Wood's hypothetical debate and explicitly restates Aron's accepted burden and evidential challenge to Wood.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This response supplies Aron's governing burden-of-proof defense of naturalism and directly contests Wood's claim that an internal critique can defeat it.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Wood's solipsism analogy and his claim that an affirmative worldview cannot be defended only by demanding that opponents prove an alternative.

candidates.contextSummary: Aron dismisses the hypothetical as unlike the agreed debate, accepts defending naturalism, and insists that disproving it requires showing a supernatural aspect that Wood has not shown.

candidates.speaker: David Wood
candidates.proposition: Naturalism warrants Humean or Darwinian agnosticism because evolved cognitive faculties directed toward survival are not trustworthy for judging ultimate reality.
candidates.attributionBasis: Wood explicitly invokes Hume and Darwin as examples and connects their skepticism to his established cognitive-reliability argument.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The move directly advances the debate's central thesis that an evolutionary-naturalist account undermines the rational confidence needed to affirm naturalism.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Aron's assertion that ordinary sensory experience must be accepted and that Wood must prove a supernatural alternative to refute naturalism.

candidates.contextSummary: Wood argues that neither Hume nor Darwin could confidently answer whether naturalism is true, because their own accounts give them reason to distrust such sweeping metaphysical judgments.

candidates.speaker: Aron Ra
candidates.proposition: Affirming the shared natural world leaves the opponent responsible for establishing a supernatural alternative, regardless of which formulation of naturalism Aron adopts.
candidates.attributionBasis: The speaker uses Aron's first-person position, affirms the shared natural world, and places the evidential burden directly on Wood.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The move directly answers the cognitive-skepticism strategy by returning the dispute to comparative evidence for anything beyond the acknowledged natural world.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Wood's appeal to Hume and Darwin as grounds for withholding affirmation of naturalism without first establishing supernaturalism.

candidates.contextSummary: Aron argues that both sides acknowledge a natural world, so whether he says it is all that exists or simply asks for more, Wood must demonstrate the proposed exception.

candidates.speaker: David Wood
candidates.proposition: Naturalism can be rationally rejected through its internal incoherence without proving supernaturalism, because its account of cognition undercuts confidence in metaphysical conclusions.
candidates.attributionBasis: Wood explicitly distinguishes internal critique from proving supernaturalism and develops his argument through Darwin, Hume, evolution, and epiphenomenalism.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This is the fullest statement in the exchange of the pro side's motion-level case that naturalism defeats the rational warrant required for its own affirmation.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Aron's repeated claim that the only relevant way to reject naturalism is to provide evidence that something supernatural exists.

candidates.contextSummary: Wood says multiple routes can defeat naturalism, then argues that evolved faculties and possibly causally inert mental states justify agnosticism about ultimate reality even without affirming another worldview.

candidates.speaker: Aron Ra
candidates.proposition: Natural explanations for apparent design are available, while Wood has supplied neither evidence nor even an indicated possibility of anything supernatural.
candidates.attributionBasis: The turn uses Aron's evidential vocabulary, corrects his own word choice, and explains apparent design through population mechanics and natural selection.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The response states the con side's central evidence-centered defense: natural mechanisms explain the observations while the proposed supernatural exception lacks support.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Wood's argument that evolutionary origins and limited cognitive purposes make it rationally improper to affirm naturalism.

candidates.contextSummary: Aron rejects the alleged conflict between naturalism and rationality, explains incidental apparent design through selection, and says Wood has offered no positive reason to consider a supernatural alternative.

candidates.speaker: David Wood
candidates.proposition: If beliefs result from causally determined particles and mental states lack causal efficacy, naturalism gives no adequate basis for trusting assessments of reality.
candidates.attributionBasis: The moderator hands the closing to Wood, who explicitly recaps his opening and develops determinism, epiphenomenalism, and evolutionary selection.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Wood's closing consolidates the principal cognitive-reliability critique by connecting physical determination, epiphenomenalism, and selection to self-defeat.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Aron's insistence that objective data and natural mechanisms justify his position while Wood has failed to establish anything supernatural.

candidates.contextSummary: In closing, Wood argues that mindless causal origins are at least as epistemically concerning as upbringing, and that survival-selected faculties and causally inert mental states cannot warrant naturalism.

candidates.speaker: David Wood
candidates.proposition: The practice of rational debate itself is more intelligible if human cognitive faculties have an origin beyond mindless particles and motion.
candidates.attributionBasis: Wood remains in his uninterrupted closing statement and presents the debate itself as evidence favoring a non-natural origin of cognition.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The move adds a positive abductive component to Wood's mainly internal critique by arguing that rational discourse fits better with a non-natural cognitive source.
candidates.contextSummary: Wood reflects on the present and other debates, claiming that reasoned disagreement makes substantially more sense if cognitive faculties originate in something beyond mindless physical processes.

candidates.speaker: Aron Ra
candidates.proposition: Bottom-up emergence and population mechanics explain apparent design, whereas supernatural and religious claims remain unverifiable, often falsified, and evidentially unsupported.
candidates.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly gives the closing to Aron, who rejects Wood's characterization and reprises his emergence and verification arguments.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Aron's closing unifies his naturalistic alternative and evidential standard, directly defending naturalism against both the design inference and supernatural contrast.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Wood's closing claim that rational cognition and debate fit better with faculties originating beyond mindless natural processes.

candidates.contextSummary: Aron answers that complex order emerges from bottom-up processes without intentional design and argues that supernatural claims never pass the staged evidential path from possibility to probability to fact.

candidates.speaker: David Wood
candidates.proposition: Supernatural causation may not be consistently measurable because any resulting event immediately becomes naturally observable and remains open to alternative natural interpretation.
candidates.attributionBasis: A question is explicitly directed to David, and the answer uses Wood's first-person examples while conceding limits on consistent supernatural measurement.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The Q&A answer is load-bearing because it addresses the con side's verification demand and explains why observable effects may not uniquely identify supernatural causation.
candidates.contextSummary: Asked how the supernatural could be measured, Wood says a miraculous effect would enter the natural record, but even strong testimonial and medical evidence could always be reinterpreted naturally.
